observation.visible_scene: A tall, narrow waterfall plunges vertically down a sheer, dark rock cliff face that is heavily covered with green moss, ferns, and shrubs, with a band of bright green treetops along the top edge. At the base of the falls, a curved rainbow arcs across the misty lower-right area over reddish-brown rock. A small 'AGG' watermark sits in the upper-left corner. The overall composition (cliff, vegetation, waterfall position, rainbow location) stays fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The white water column is in continuous downward flow: the internal streaks, swirls, and turbulent texture of the falling water shift and churn from frame to frame, indicating steady motion rather than a static image.
The width and silhouette of the water column remain roughly constant top-to-bottom; it does not visibly expand, contract, or translate sideways—only its surface texture changes as water descends.
The mist and rainbow at the base persist across all frames, with only subtle, gradual variation in the brightness and exact shape of the rainbow band as the spray drifts.
The cliff face, vegetation, and treetops show no positional change, and the 'AGG' watermark remains fixed, indicating the camera is essentially static during this segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: The water source above the cliff edge and the plunge pool / river below the rainbow are not shown.
Whether the flow rate or rainbow intensity changes outside this short window is unknown; the segment only captures an ongoing, steady state.
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift or micro-zoom is not clearly distinguishable from the static background.
Small apparent shifts in the rainbow's position may be due to changing mist rather than the rainbow itself moving.
